report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-07 starting around 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC), assistant replies experienced latency degradation from ~6.5 seconds to 24-25.5 seconds, with a small percentage of user requests failing with generic error messages ('Something went wrong'). Investigation revealed that external llm-provider began throttling requests to model lumen-large-2026-08 with HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'. Baseline orchestrator traffic (~211k-267k TPM) exceeded this quota, triggering exponential backoff retries (up to 3 attempts with 2-8s backoff) that inflated response times and resulted in fallback error messages upon retry exhaustion. A concurrent knowledge index rebuild (build 4121) kicked off at 11:00 IST (05:30 UTC) was investigated and ruled out.
report.rootCauseStatement: At 05:50:04 UTC (11:20:04 IST), external llm-provider began returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000') for model lumen-large-2026-08. Assistant-orchestrator's baseline traffic of 211,000–267,000 tokens per minute exceeded this quota, causing rate-limited calls to spike from 0 to over 55-79/min and triggering client-side exponential backoff retries (26-66 retries/min). Cumulative retry delays inflated p95 conversation latency past 20 seconds, and conversations that exhausted all 3 retry attempts failed with fallback generic error responses.

hypotheses.cause: External llm-provider enforced or reduced an account token quota limit of 200,000 tokens per minute (TPM) on model lumen-large-2026-08 starting at 05:50 UTC. Baseline assistant-orchestrator traffic (211,000–267,000 TPM) was throttled with HTTP 429, causing exponential backoff retries that inflated conversation latency to 20+ seconds and generated fallback error responses when retries were exhausted.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct log messages starting at 05:50:04 UTC confirm HTTP 429 with 'quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000'. Prior to 05:50 UTC, orchestrator token consumption ran between 211,000 and 267,000 TPM without 429 errors. Retry storms directly account for the ~17-18s increase in LLM call latency and orchestrator p95 latency.

hypotheses.cause: Knowledge index rebuild build 4121 (CHG-48222) started at 05:30 UTC degraded knowledge-index search latency or consumed LLM quota, slowing down assistant conversations.
hypotheses.rationale: Knowledge-index latency only rose from ~85ms to ~369ms, well below the orchestrator's 800ms timeout, and error rates remained flat at ~0.10%. Furthermore, dependency analysis confirmed neither indexing-pipeline nor knowledge-index calls llm-provider.

hypotheses.cause: An unmonitored external client, internal script, or secondary service sharing the organization's llm-provider API key began issuing requests at ~05:50 UTC, exhausting a pre-existing 200,000 TPM account-level token quota and starving assistant-orchestrator.
hypotheses.rationale: Assistant-orchestrator was the only internal service in the assistant domain configured with a dependency on llm-provider. However, absence of provider-side per-key request breakdown prevents entirely ruling out an external or uncatalogued script.

facts.statement: assistant-orchestrator overall request latency (latency_p95_ms) jumped from baseline levels of 6,188–6,768 ms prior to 05:50 UTC up to 12,765 ms at 05:50 UTC, and reached 23,299–25,578 ms from 05:55 UTC onward.
assistant-orchestrator downstream LLM call latency (llm_latency_p95_ms) rose from baseline levels of 4,990–5,466 ms to 11,252 ms at 05:50 UTC, and sustained 22,152–23,347 ms from 05:55 UTC onward.

assistant-orchestrator retry_count jumped from 0.4–1.2 retries/min prior to 05:50 UTC to 26.47/min at 05:50 UTC and 48–66 retries/min thereafter, while rate_limited_count surged from ~0 to 33.38/min at 05:50 UTC and 55–79/min thereafter.

At 2026-10-07T05:50:04.497Z, assistant-orchestrator began logging warnings stating 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000); retrying in Xs (attempt Y/3)' for model lumen-large-2026-08.

Starting at 2026-10-07T05:52:02Z, assistant-orchestrator logged errors showing conversations failed after 3 retry attempts due to llm-provider 429 and returned fallback messages ('Something went wrong') to users.
assistant-orchestrator token consumption was 211,912–267,782 tokens/min prior to 05:50 UTC, and decreased to 164,350–185,502 tokens/min after 05:50 UTC as requests were throttled.
indexing-pipeline has downstream dependencies only on knowledge-index and message-queue, and knowledge-index has zero downstream dependencies; neither calls llm-provider.
knowledge-index index_version remained at 4120, docs_count remained constant at 18,450, error_rate stayed at 0.08–0.12%, and p95 retrieval latency peaked at 369.3 ms during background build 4121.
assistant-orchestrator timeout configuration is 800 ms (0 retries) to knowledge-index, and 25,000 ms (2 retries) to llm-provider.
user-context-service and portfolio-service p95 latencies remained stable at ~175 ms and ~143 ms respectively, with normal error rates throughout the incident window.

inferences.statement: The 20+ second overall orchestrator response latency is directly driven by downstream LLM call latency and retry delays, rather than context retrieval or knowledge search.

Because assistant-orchestrator previously operated at 211,000 to 267,000 tokens per minute between 05:00 and 05:45 UTC without any 429 responses, the 200,000 TPM quota limit was newly enforced or reduced on the account by llm-provider at 05:50 UTC.

The concurrent knowledge index rebuild (build 4121) was not the cause of the assistant latency spikes or error responses because its search latency increase was negligible (peaking at ~369 ms vs 800 ms timeout) and it has no dependency on llm-provider.

assumptions.statement: The 200,000 TPM limit reported in the 429 error message reflects an account- or model-tier quota enforced by the external provider rather than an internal gateway throttle.

timeline.event: Change CHG-48222 initiates a full knowledge index rebuild (build 4121) for embedding model refresh; indexing-pipeline begins background embedding.
knowledge-index retrieval latency p95 elevates slightly from ~85 ms to ~340-369 ms; assistant-orchestrator latency remains normal at ~6.2-6.4 s and 0 rate-limiting errors.
llm-provider begins returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('quota exceeded: tokens per minute, limit=200000') on model lumen-large-2026-08.
assistant-orchestrator rate-limited requests surge to 33-70/min and retries surge to 26-57/min; orchestrator p95 latency jumps to 12.8 s and then 24.1 s.
First conversation failures logged after exhausting 3 retry attempts against llm-provider, returning fallback error responses to end users.
Assistant team on-call receives user reports and logs SEV2 incident INC-5200.

confidence.rationale: High confidence supported by unmasked orchestrator warning and error logs showing the explicit HTTP 429 error payload specifying 'limit=200000' tokens per minute, exact timestamp correlation at 05:50:04 UTC with latency and retry spikes, and complete exoneration of alternative hypotheses (knowledge-index, user-context-service, portfolio-service).

gaps.impact: Minimal impact on immediate root cause determination, but needed for vendor review and post-incident accounting.

recommendedActions.action: Contact llm-provider support or account manager immediately to request a quota increase for model lumen-large-2026-08 from 200,000 TPM to at least 500,000 TPM to comfortably accommodate peak baseline traffic.
recommendedActions.rationale: Baseline orchestrator traffic requires 250,000 to 270,000 TPM; the 200,000 TPM limit directly bottlenecks production assistant operations.
recommendedActions.verification: Check assistant-orchestrator metric rate_limited_count drops to 0/min and llm_latency_p95_ms recovers to baseline ~5.0-5.5s.

recommendedActions.action: Configure a fallback secondary model or provider in assistant-orchestrator when receiving HTTP 429 quota exhaustion from the primary model.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents user-facing retry storms and conversation failures when single-model quotas are breached.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate 429 response in staging and verify orchestrator gracefully routes to secondary model without inflating p95 latency past 10s.

recommendedActions.action: Implement proactive alerting on assistant-orchestrator token consumption approaching account quota thresholds (e.g., alert at 80% of configured TPM limit).
recommendedActions.rationale: Provides advance warning to on-call engineers before user conversations experience throttling and retry backoff delays.

recommendedActions.rationale: Eliminates noisy neighbor risks from external or batch workloads exhausting production serving quotas.
